transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-27 14:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood Solutions), Tom Whitaker (Archipelago Head of Search), Priya Desai (Archipelago ML Eng), Jonas Meyer (Product), Zoe (intern)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): quick hosted API demo showing embeddings endpoint and reranker endpoint for product search. Discussed latency vs cost, candidate generation + rerank pattern, evaluation metrics (MRR/NDCG), and enterprise security (SOC2, SSO, VPC). Agreed to pilot and exchange sample vectors.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros, we'll do a 25-ish minute demo and then leave time for questions and a short next-steps recap. Tom, do you want to kick off with your goals?
[00:18] Tom (Archipelago): Sure, thanks. We're trying to replace a brittle hybrid of ES + hand-coded boosting. Main issues are inconsistent results for long-tail queries and high ops on the ranking side. We want something that improves relevance with minimal infra lift — latency requirements are around 200ms p95 for the storefront, budget is, uh, ~ $X per month for search.
[00:35] Priya (Archipelago): And we have about 5–10M SKUs, cold start is a problem. We use HNSW index now and Pinecone for some experiments, but cost is creeping up. Interested in how Redwood's hosted API could act as both embedding store + rerank step.
[00:51] Mateo (Redwood SE): Great context. We'll show a typical pattern: candidate generation via vector similarity on 1536-d embeddings, then a lightweight reranker model call that uses full product metadata and query context to reorder top-K. We'll demo both the embeddings endpoint and the reranker endpoint on our hosted API.
[01:12] Zoe (intern): Quick question, what are the embedding dims you support?
[01:18] Aisha (Redwood): Depends on model, common sizes we demo are 512 and 1536. For ecomm we usually recommend 1536 for semantic fidelity, but Optimize can suggest quantized profiles to reduce footprint.
[01:30] Jonas (Archipelago): You're recommending hosted or dedicated? Our compliance asks are getting stricter.
[01:35] Lena: Good question. Hosted is fastest to launch; Dedicated gives reserved capacity and VPC peering options and is cheaper at scale. Private (on-prem/VPC) is also available for strict residency. We'll include a side-by-side in the follow-up.
[01:50] (demo start) Mateo: I'm going to share my screen — apologies if the share quality is rough. First, the console overview: you can create an index, upload vectors in batches via the embeddings endpoint, and see ingestion metrics per batch. Here in the console we have a sample 'archipelago-catalog' index with 1M vectors.
[02:12] Mateo: API snippet: POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-1536 and inputs=[...]. You get back base64 vectors, or the API returns floats depending on client. If you want to store them in your vector DB you can send raw floats or compressed.
[02:35] Priya: How do you handle batching? We often have daily bulk jobs.
[02:40] Mateo: We recommend batching at 1k vectors per request for throughput; Optimize can suggest the sweet spot based on your token distribution and model. There's automatic retry and chunking in SDKs.
[02:55] Tom: What about nearest neighbor search — do you provide that or do we use our vector DB?
[03:01] Lena: Hosted API provides similarity endpoints for small/medium index sizes for convenience. For 5–10M we usually recommend an external vector store (your HNSW) + run Redwood reranker on top. The typical flow we demo: 1) candidate generation via your vector DB (Pinecone/HNSW) using 100 nearest; 2) call Redwood reranker endpoint with query + top-K product metadata to return final ranking.
[03:26] (short crosstalk) Jonas: That fits our architecture — we keep index in DB but want inference quality improvement.
[03:34] Mateo: I'll run a live rerank example. Note: the reranker endpoint accepts a JSON payload with query, candidate list, and optional user signals. It returns scores and an ordered array. For demo, I'm using a 12-item top-K; in production we often do 50 then rerank 10–12 to balance cost/latency.
[03:58] [03:58] Mateo: (typing) Sending request... Response in 120ms. Here you can see the before/after ordering and an explain score breakdown per feature — the console shows token-level contribution, similarity boost, price preference, and promotions weight.
[04:20] Priya: 120ms is great. What's the p95 for rerank at 10 items?
[04:26] Mateo: On hosted small instances, p95 ~ 150–220ms depending on model size; on dedicated with optimized kernels we see p95 <120ms. We'll share precise perf numbers for the specific model variants.
[04:40] Tom: And cost implications — we might get a lot of queries. How do you charge?
[04:46] Lena: Hosted is per-embedding-unit and per-rerank call; we'll send a pricing estimate for your expected QPS. For high volume, Dedicated reserved pools are more cost effective — we can model TCO for 6/12/24 month commitments.
[05:00] Priya: On the reranker, do you use cross-encoder style models? How do you avoid token explosion with long product descriptions?
[05:07] Mateo: Good catch. Our reranker uses a candidate-aware model that encodes query + truncated product text and metadata features (category, brand, price). We apply adaptive truncation and optional embeddings for long fields. For very long descriptions we can index summaries or use a two-stage approach with coarse semantic match followed by fine cross-encoder for top-5.
[05:32] Tom: Can you do A/B tests or rollout? We want canary and quick rollback if quality regresses.
[05:37] Aisha: The Console has built-in rollout controls: you can configure canary percentages, route by region or user segment, and automatic fallback to previous model if latency or quality SLOs drop. Also ties into our Optimize suite which can recommend batch/quantization settings to meet cost SLOs.
[05:55] Priya: Security — log retention, encryption, SSO?
[06:00] Lena: We are SOC 2 Type II; we support SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. Hosted retains logs for 30 days by default and you can opt out or set custom retention for enterprise. For strict requirements we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS and audit logs sent to your SIEM. I'll send the security pack after the call.
[06:20] (demo continues) Mateo: Back to rerank: I'm going to show an eval run. We upload a small eval set of queries and use the Console's Eval page. It reports MRR, NDCG@10, and precision at 1. You can also attach human labels and do pairwise comparisons.
[06:38] Mateo: Here we ran archipelago-sample-500 with baseline (your current ES ranker) vs Redwood reranker. NDCG improved from 0.62 to 0.74 in this sample, and click-through simulated lift about +8%. These are illustrative but the pipeline is typical.
[06:55] Tom: Nice. What about explainability — product teams need to justify ranking changes.
[07:01] Mateo: The Console provides per-query explanations: feature importance bars, contribution from similarity vs business rules. Those can be exported as CSV for audits.
[07:12] Priya: For embeddings, do you support incremental updates? We have frequent catalog churn.
[07:18] Aisha: Yes, incremental upserts are supported. The SDK also has a delta-upsert helper that does chunking and retries; Optimize can recommend a refresh cadence to balance freshness vs compute.
[07:30] Jonas: Any rate limits? We plan bursts during promotions.
[07:33] Lena: Hosted has quota controls and burst capacity options; Dedicated can be configured to handle sustained bursts. We also support priority routing for certain keys.
[07:43] (brief pause) Priya: Edge cases — promotions, personalization per user — can rerank include user signals?
[07:52] Mateo: Yes, you can pass user features and recent interactions with each candidate. The model scores them; you can also add rule-based overrides (e.g., boost for sponsored items). The reranker supports both ML and deterministic feature inputs.
[08:10] Tom: For evaluation, what's the recommended size to get reliable signals?
[08:13] Mateo: For relevance metrics we recommend at least 1k labeled queries for initial sanity checks; for robust statistical significance 5k+. We can help seed labeling and run a paired-A/B test in prod.
[08:25] (noise on line; speaker label missing) Speaker 1: sorry, small audio glitch.
[08:30] (demo - code walkthrough) Mateo: Here's a quick SDK snippet in Python. from redwood import Client; cli = Client(api_key=...); idx.upsert(vectors); results = db.search(query_vec, top_k=100); reranked = client.rerank(query, candidates=results) — simple.
[08:48] Priya: That looks straightforward. Do you provide connectors to common vector DBs?
[08:52] Aisha: We have example connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, and Elastic vector search; community-contrib for others.
[08:58] Jonas: Latency budget again — if we route candidate search to our HNSW cluster in GCP and then call Redwood reranker in us-west, any cold network issues?
[09:07] Mateo: We recommend colocating reranker near your DB region to minimize egress. For Hosted we have multi-region endpoints and will route by policy. Also we provide a caching layer so repeated queries hit cached rerank results for TTL-defined queries (e.g., exact match or heavy queries).
[09:25] Priya: Can we persist reranker features for offline analysis?
[09:29] Mateo: Yes, you can export logs and features. For Dedicated/Private you can push logs to your storage.
[09:36] Tom: Any sample customers in retail?
[09:38] Lena: We've worked with a few mid-market retailers; happy to share anonymized benchmarks.
[09:44] Tom: Ok show me the Optimize suggestions — you mentioned quantization.
[09:48] Mateo: Optimize looks at your workload (sequence lengths, QPS) and recommends model variants, quantization (e.g., 8-bit), and batching settings. For embeddings we sometimes recommend a quantized 1536->int8 profile for storage reduction and keep reranker at float16 for accuracy.
[10:05] Priya: Is there recompression support between storage and runtime?
[10:09] Aisha: We support on-the-fly decompress/float conversion in the runtime to avoid repeated conversions. That said, it depends on the client flow.
[10:18] (questions from Jonas) Jonas: If we see quality regressions post-deploy, what's rollback process?
[10:22] Mateo: Canary route with metrics: if NDCG or latency breaches thresholds, automatic rollback occurs. You can also schedule night-time rollouts.
[10:30] Tom: On data privacy — if we send product text that includes PII (supply chain IDs), do you retain that?
[10:36] Lena: Default retention is 30 days for logs; embeddings and payloads can be not stored if you set no-retain mode. For regulated data, Private deployment is best.
[10:45] Priya: Any offline benchmarking you can run for us?
[10:48] Mateo: Yes — action item: share sample vectors and queries and we'll run a baseline and rerank eval; expect a report within ~7 days.
[11:00] (recap and next steps) Lena: Recap: we'll send SOC2 + security pack, pricing scenarios, and provision trial API keys. Archipelago will share 5k sample vectors and a set of labeled queries. Mateo will run the rerank baseline and share NDCG/MRR results.
[11:20] Tom: Sounds good. A couple of small asks: can you show infra TCO for 6/12 months?
[11:26] Lena: Yes, pricing grid incoming.
[11:30] Priya: Also share example SDK ingestion scripts and the connector for our HNSW setup.
[11:35] Lena: We'll include them.
[11:38] Jonas: Any blocker on doing the pilot next week?
[11:41] Lena: We can start initial provisioning next week pending NDA — I think this timeline is fine.
[11:47] (call closing) Lena: Thanks all, we'll follow up with a one-pager and links.
[11:52] (end)
